notes: Web 409 - LANDSCAPE-MODE-NOV10 (owner, Nov 10, 2026 13:59 CST: "why is the app not working in landscape mode? either on the GPS nor on the application it should be"). Two convictions, both measured in a real engine at 915x412 against live-408 bytes. (1) THE LOCK: the only hard orientation lock in either repo was the WEB APP MANIFEST - assets/manifest.json declared "orientation": "portrait", which Android enforces on the installed web app (window held portrait, rotation does nothing). The native shell carries no lock (merged gen-76 APK manifest: MainActivity has no screenOrientation, configChanges covers orientation, resizeableActivity=true; no requestedOrientation call in the native sources). Fix: manifest orientation portrait -> any. (2) THE BREAKAGE: with rotation allowed, the Navigator PLANNING face still failed sideways - its map carries two absolutely-positioned overlay stacks (.nv-map-top search+kind ~154px, .nv-map-bottom banner+mode ~157-261px) needing ~415px of vertical room; a landscape phone's mapzone is ~232px, so the stacks overlapped 99-180px and buried each other (portrait's ~717px mapzone never collides). Fix: inside the existing v300 landscape block only, each stack is capped and scrolls internally (.nv-map-top max-height:52%; .nv-map-bottom max-height:calc(48% - 20px)) - the two can never meet at any height, every control stays reachable, and where the stacks already fit (Fold open, ~545px mapzone) the caps never bind. Portrait untouched. Verified already-working sideways and unchanged: dashboard + tracker card, and the Navigator DRIVE face (v300 compact banner engages: 899x52 flex row, bar, speed cluster bottom-left). Bench: tools/landscape-mode-nov10-test.js failing-first on web-408 bytes 3 passed / 7 failed (exactly S1-S5 + the E2/E3 geometry) -> 10/10 on the fix; nav neighbours at pristine standings (navigator-screen 38/2, nav-inset-topright-v237 15/4, monday-fix-v300 39/1 - identical before and after). Native pointer preserved (76 / meticulous-v76.apk); webVersion 408 -> 409; pin style.css 396 -> 409. No native change: no gen 77. IN-HANDS VERDICT OWED: on the truck mount, sideways - the installed web app must now rotate; the Navigator's planning controls must sit apart and scroll within their stacks instead of burying each other; portrait must look exactly as before. If rotation still refuses in the native app after this, the remaining suspect is the phone's own auto-rotate setting - the app side carries no lock anywhere.
